001_Studio.name: OrientOffset
001_Studio.desc: Applies a matrix orient offset setup to a list of custom controls.
001_Studio.help:
Overview:
  Applies the matrix orient offset setup to a custom list of controls.

How To Use:
  Select the controls in the scene and click 'Add Selected' below. Then click build.

Fields:
- SetControlsList: List of controls to process.
- AutoParentChildren: If true, existing children of the controls will be reparented under the new _Driven groups automatically.
- RemapScaleConnections: If true, detects direct scale connections going out of the control (e.g. multiplyDivide nodes from ScaleTweakCtrls) and remaps them through the orient rotation so scale axes match the new visual orientation.
- HideOrientAttrs: If true, the proxy orient attributes on the control will be hidden on build.
- LockOrientAttrs: If true, the proxy orient attributes on the control will be locked on build.

001_Studio.name: MirrorNodeEachSide
001_Studio.desc: Finds Mirror_Grp nodes on one side and creates matching mirror groups on the opposite side
001_Studio.help:
Overview:
  Finds all nodes ending with Mirror_Grp and creates matching mirror groups on the opposite side.

How It Works:
  1. Searches the scene for any node ending with Mirror_Grp (e.g. R_Antenna_A_Ctrl_Offset_GrpMirror_Grp).
  2. Strips the Mirror_Grp suffix to get the base name (R_Antenna_A_Ctrl_Offset_Grp).
  3. Swaps the R_ prefix to L_ (or vice versa) to find the opposite-side node.
  4. Creates a new group (L_Antenna_A_Ctrl_Offset_GrpMirror_Grp) at the origin.
  5. Inserts it above the opposite-side node so it becomes a child of the new group.

Fields:
- RunAfterBuild: Check True to defer execution until after the full build finishes (recommended if the Mirror_Grp nodes are generated by later blocks).

Tips:
- Build this block after all mirrored rig components are in place.
- The new mirror groups are created with identity transforms (at origin).

001_Studio.name: SetDefaults
001_Studio.desc: Captures selected channel box attributes and their values, then restores them on build.
001_Studio.help:
Overview:
  Captures selected channel box attributes and their current values, storing them for rebuild.

How To Use:
  1. Create the block (no selection needed).
  2. Select objects in the viewport and highlight attributes in the Channel Box.
  3. Click Add to store those attribute values.
  4. Select entries and click Remove to delete them.
  5. On Build, those stored values will be set back on the controls.

Fields:
- RunAfterBuild: Check True to defer execution until after the full build finishes (recommended if attributes are built by later blocks).
- SetDefaultsList: List of node.attr = value entries.

Tips:
- Each entry is stored as node.attr = value.
- Supports any numeric attribute (float, int, bool, enum).
- You can add from multiple objects across multiple Add actions.

001_Studio.name: AnimCtrlRename
001_Studio.desc: Renames animation controls and all their related nodes (shapes, constraints, offset groups, etc.) based on a search-and-replace list.
001_Studio.help:
Overview:
  Renames animation controls and all their related nodes (shapes, constraints, offset groups, etc.) based on a search-and-replace list.

How To Use:
  1. Create the block.
  2. Paste a two-column spreadsheet (old_name and new_name) or select controls and click Add Selected.
  3. Double-click any entry in the list to edit it manually if needed.
  4. When you click Build, all controls and their related constraints/shapes will be renamed safely.

Fields:
- RunBeforeBuild: Check True to run renaming before the main build begins.
- RunAfterBuild: Check True to defer execution until after the full build finishes (so shape files and skins are loaded first before renaming).
- Revert: Check True to reverse the renaming direction (e.g. for entry old = new, 'new' will be renamed to 'old').
- RenameList: List of old_name = new_name entries.

001_Studio.name: VisAttrs
001_Studio.desc: Creates visibility attributes (Off/On enum) on a target control and connects them to the visibility of specified nodes.
001_Studio.help:
Overview:
  Creates visibility enum attributes (Off/On) on a target control and connects them to the visibility of specified nodes.

How To Use:
  1. Create the block.
  2. Select the control that will hold the visibility attributes, and click 'Add Selected' or type its name in SetTargetCtrl.
  3. In VisAttrsList, specify the attribute name and the driven nodes in the format:
     AttrName = Node1, Node2
     Example:
     Hair = L_Hair_Geo, R_Hair_Geo
     Jacket = Jacket_Geo
  4. When you click Build, the attributes will be added to the target control and connected to the nodes' visibility.

Fields:
- SetTargetCtrl: The control that will hold the visibility attributes.
- VisAttrsList: List of entries in the format: AttrName = Node1, Node2
- DefaultOn: If True, attributes will default to On. If False, they will default to Off.

001_Studio.name: Pickwalk
001_Studio.desc: Imports pickwalk attributes from a JSON file and applies quickPick direction links to rig controls.
001_Studio.help:
Overview:
  Imports pickwalk (quickPick) direction attributes from a JSON file and applies them to rig controls.

How To Use:
  1. Create the block.
  2. Set the PickwalkFile field to the path of your pickwalk JSON file, or click Browse to select one.
  3. Click Build to import and apply the pickwalk attributes.

Fields:
- PickwalkFile: Path to the pickwalk JSON file containing quickPick direction attributes.

JSON Format:
  The file should contain a dictionary of control names mapped to their quickPick attributes:
  { "Ctrl_Name": { "quickPick_left": "Other_Ctrl", "quickPick_right": "Another_Ctrl" } }

Tips:
- Use the pickwalk export tools to generate the JSON file from an existing rig.
- Attributes are created if they don't exist, or updated if they do.

001_Studio.name: SculptDeformer
001_Studio.desc: Sculpt Deformer with control and mirror support
001_Studio.help:
Overview:
  Sculpt Deformer with control, two locators (sculptor + stretch origin), and mirror support.

How To Use:
  Fill in the fields below then build.

Fields:
- SetGeo: comma-separated list of target geometry names.
- SetParent: parent node for the built rig. If left as 'new_locator', a placeholder locator is created.
- Mirror: False builds as-is. True builds both L_ and R_ sides (auto-prefixes L_ if needed). Right_Only builds only the R_ side mirrored from the guide.
- CtrlSize: size of the control curve (default 1).
- CtrlColor: color of the control curve.
- Scale: comma-separated XYZ scale for the sculpt deformer (default 10,1,10 for flattening).

Tips:
- When Mirror is True, R_ side SetGeo names are auto-derived by replacing L_ with R_.
- The sculptor locator drives the deformer position; the stretch origin sets the sculpt stretch origin.
- Template parent examples: Spine_End_Jnt, Head_Jnt, L_Wrist_Jnt.

008_Props.name: Ribbon
008_Props.desc: Creates a ribbon, Copyright (C) 2018 Orkhan Ashrafov
008_Props.help:
Overview:
  Creates a ribbon, Copyright (C) 2018 Orkhan Ashrafov.

How To Use:
  fill the key fields below before build.

Fields:
- SetParent: set the target node name.
- If left as default, the tool uses placeholder behavior for setup.
- Mirror: True builds both L_ and R_ sides (auto-prefixes L_ if needed). Right_Only mirrors to the right side only. False builds as-is.
- Equal: evenly spaces controls and joints along the ribbon. When OFF, spacing follows the surface parameterization.
- Ctrls: number of IK controls along the ribbon (default 5).
- Joints: number of bind joints along the ribbon (default 5).
- Constraint: ON uses parentConstraint/scaleConstraint to link IK controls to their joints (supports offsets, more flexible). OFF uses direct attribute connections (lighter, no constraint overhead).
- AddFk: adds an FK control chain on top of the IK controls for layered animation.
- FkOnLast: when ON (and AddFk is ON), adds an FK control on the final IK control as well. Default is OFF, which skips the last control.
- Wire: uses a wire deformer instead of a skinCluster to drive the ribbon surface. Needs at least 2 controls.
- CtrlScales: when ON, unlocks scale attributes on the IK controls and connects them to the bind joints.
- JointOrient: when ON, bind joints orient to the nearest control joint instead of the follicle surface normal.
- MiddleCtrlPosition: where the main control is placed. Original uses the surface bounding box center. Start/End places it at the first/last bind joint.
- CtrlOrientation: SurfaceNormal keeps the default follicle orientation (Z follows surface normal). WorldForward orients controls and joints so Z faces world-forward and Y faces world-up.
- Gimbal: adds a nested gimbal control under the Ribbon Main Control for clean rotations.
- Template parent examples: Spine_End_Jnt, Head_Jnt, L_Wrist_Jnt.

Tips:
- if a field says left/right or mirror, use it to generate the opposite side quickly.

How To Use:

Fields:
- SetJoints: Comma-separated list of joints/objects to create controllers on.
- SetParent: Node the ctrl offset group will follow via parentConstraint (mo=True).
  Default is Ctrl_Grp. Leave empty to skip the constraint.
- Shape: Curve shape for the controller.
- Color: Override color for the controller.
- Scale: Size multiplier (1-20).
- Connection: How to connect the ctrl to the joint.
  * DirectConnect: connectAttr ctrl.t/r/s -> joint.t/r/s.
  * ParentConstraint: joint follows ctrl via parentConstraint (mo=True).
  * ScaleConnect: joint scale follows ctrl scale via connectAttr.
  * ParentAndScale: parentConstraint + scale connectAttr.
  * None: no connection, ctrl is just positioned at the joint.
- StripJointSuffix: strips _Jnt suffix before adding _Ctrl.
  Example: L_Arm_Jnt -> L_Arm_Ctrl. If False: L_Arm_Jnt_Ctrl.

- DirectConnect is the default and most direct wiring.
- ParentAndScale is preferred when you need mo offset flexibility.

  2. Add the target controls/groups to the Controls list in the same order you want them to be constrained.
  3. Each vertex will drive the corresponding control/group in the same position in the lists.
  4. Constraints will be created on offset groups (not directly on the input controls).

- Vertices (SetNodeList): list of vertex components (mesh.vtx[index] format) added in selection order.
- Controls (SetControls): list of control/group names to constrain.
- MinWeight: minimum influence weight threshold to keep.

Tips:
- Use the Add Selected button to append vertices in the order you select them.
- Use the Add Selected button in the Controls list to add controls/groups in the order you want them to match the vertices.
- Ensure all geometry is properly skinned before building.
- Controls/groups must exist in the scene.
